sources.entry: Python: _A Reasoning Model (LLM with inference-time scaling, GRPO and distillation)_

summary.one_liner: A companion code repository for the book "Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch)," which adds reasoning capabilities to a pre-trained Qwen3 base LLM step by step in Python notebooks.
summary.what_it_does: The repository holds the code for the Manning book on building reasoning LLMs. It starts from a pre-trained open-source base model (Qwen3) and implements reasoning methods in code, covering text generation, evaluation on MATH-500, inference-time scaling (chain-of-thought prompting, self-consistency, best-of-N, self-refinement), reinforcement learning with GRPO, and distillation. Chapters are organized as folders with main and exercise-solution notebooks, plus appendices on larger LLMs, batching, evaluation approaches, and a chat interface. Optional bonus material includes GRPO scripts, distillation data generation via Ollama or OpenRouter, and checkpoints usable with Hugging Face transformers. The README says the code loads weights of existing pretrained models.
use_cases: learn how reasoning LLMs work by coding them
experiment with inference-time scaling on math problems
run GRPO reinforcement learning on a small LLM
distill reasoning traces from a teacher model
evaluate a reasoning model on MATH-500
follow along with the Build a Reasoning Model book
how_to_run: See Chapter 2 of the book for Python and package setup tips
Open the chapter notebooks (for example ch02_main.ipynb) in each chapter's folder and run them
stack: Ollama and OpenRouter (bonus distillation data generation)
notable: Hands-on, step-by-step build of reasoning methods tied to a print book
Covers inference-time scaling, GRPO reinforcement learning, and distillation
Uses a pre-trained Qwen3 base model rather than training from nothing
Includes exercise solutions and optional bonus scripts for batched GRPO and distillation
Runs mostly on consumer hardware; code uses a GPU automatically when available
caveats: Companion code for a print book; the README says main chapter code is not accepting content extensions to stay consistent with the book
Chapters 5 and 6 are recommended to run on a GPU to replicate the results
README does not state a software license
